Enterprise agent platforms (the most detailed multi-company production write-up in months — Lyft at 270,000 AI Assist interactions/month and 65% deflection, Super TOBi at ~9.5M customers and 82% resolution, LATAM's Concierge on 3–5% margins; Databricks extends free Genie usage six months, which is what you do when agent-product adoption is behind plan)

Agent SDKs & harnesses (the harness-of-harnesses is now its own category — omnigent orchestrates other harnesses; LongHorizon-Harness ships an AgentAdapter that makes model and harness backends interchangeable without touching their native loops; the harness thesis surfaced independently for a third consecutive day)

Implementation & services revenue (the number that matters in the CX write-up is organisational, not architectural — configurable agents initialised from a JSON config plus a domain expert's prompt took build time from ~6 months to ~2 weeks, after which 'the platform was no longer the primary constraint; prompt and evaluation quality were')

Context engineering (long-horizon execution reframed as task-state management rather than a context problem — a manager picks the subtask, a fresh-context executor runs it, a read-only auditor verifies the environment before the next round, lifting Qwen 3.7-Plus 51.8% → 80.7% on WeaveBench)

AI platform distribution (Salesforce commerce telemetry puts agentic search up 200% as purchase journeys start inside assistants; the model-router category is the quiet compounder — OmniRoute +882 at 290+ providers, opencodex as a universal provider proxy)

Agent SDKs & harnesses (the harness thesis surfaces for a fourth consecutive day and from three independent directions at once — Lilian Weng's harness-engineering post hits the HN front page, Dex Horthy who coined 'context engineering' pushes past it to harness and loop engineering, and Simon Willison's LLM release makes reasoning traces and server-side tool calls a single local log store for reproducible agent debugging)

Agent skills wave (SkillTrace routes queries over an explicit query-skill graph rather than a packaged bundle, which is the composition question packaging leaves open; otherwise the topic's main channel went dark — GitHub served stale trending boards all run, so obsidian-skills, agentskills and scientific-agent-skills produced no measurable movement today)

Implementation & services revenue (the labour side of the trade shows up in the Swiss job file — the forward-deployed-engineer title has spanned Team Lead to zero-years-required inside one country in one week, and the newest posting names no LLM, RAG, prompt or agent requirement at all, listing Claude and Gemini in the benefits stack beside Kubernetes and Postgres)

Context engineering (the man who coined the term now says it is the wrong frame — Dex Horthy pushes past context engineering to harness and loop engineering, the durable leverage being the wrapper around the model rather than the prompt; and the failure mode gets named precisely on LinkedIn, an explicit guardrail surviving until the conversation grows long enough that summarisation renders it vague)

AI platform distribution (the largest forced migration from a deterministic voice assistant to an LLM one yet attempted — Gemini fully replaces Assistant on phones, tablets, Wear OS, headphones and Android Auto from 4 September, on the order of a billion devices, with no way to switch back; distribution also moves through acquisitions, with Enkrypt's controls reaching ChatGPT Enterprise customers via Anaconda)

Agent skills wave (two arXiv papers on the same day ask whether models can actually invoke and compose packaged skills inside a harness and whether they spread across distinct skills at all - the empirical question sitting under the entire repo boom; five skills repos hold trending slots simultaneously, mattpocock adds +4,503 in two days on an accelerating 7d rate, and vertical packs like scientific-agent-skills are the second wave)

Agent SDKs & harnesses (four independent sources converge on the same claim in one day - OneDayAgent targets a full day of autonomous operation rather than a task episode, Muse Code ships persistent async background agents, and an HN front-page post and a Medium essay both name the harness (scheduling, context assembly, tool mediation, policy enforcement) as the engineering discipline with the model as the swappable part; loopx enters as a 'loop engineering state kernel' at +847 from a 3,062 base)

Implementation & services revenue (the last-mile thesis gets a matching JD - Orange Business puts 'advising C-level stakeholders on AI strategy, governance, and roadmaps' inside an engineering role, which is the same claim a French practitioner tribune makes from the other side: raw model capability has become a commodity and the contest is decided after the demo; SAP's proof point is a customer cutting HR cycle times 40-60%)

Context engineering (the frame is being renamed in real time - three of today's Medium pieces on it argue the durable layer is the harness rather than the context window: compress conversation history, offload large tool results to a filesystem instead of the prompt, isolate subagent context, keep a retrieval path back to the original evidence; the topic's own territory is being annexed by 'AI control plane')

AI platform distribution (a hyperscaler claiming the agent-runtime layer is the structurally significant item of the day - cloudflare/computer is the #1 daily star gainer on all of GitHub at +2,802 from a 5,010 base; underneath it the quiet compounder is routing and reach, OmniRoute +2,314 fronting 290+ providers and a Show HN SDK for putting any agent into Slack and Teams, while IBM pilots an eCommerce surface for buying partner-built agents)

Context engineering (LangChain publishes concrete thresholds instead of generalities — tool responses over 20,000 tokens offloaded to the filesystem and replaced with a path plus a 10-line preview, old write/edit arguments truncated to file pointers at 85% of the window, summarization only when offloading is exhausted; the transferable idea is the eval methodology, deliberately triggering compression at 10-25% of the window to manufacture enough events to compare implementations, with goal drift as the worst failure mode)
